source_refs.note: Topic 6.4.1.1 Core Principles (PDF 162-163, printed 159-160). The book says consensus needs a 'unanimous decision'; it needs a sufficient majority: shown as printed, marked, with a Book correction box. MCQ 13 and short question 2 are answered. Recorded.

items: Decentralization: a network of computers (nodes) maintains the blockchain instead of a central authority, reducing the risk of a single point of failure.
Immutability: once a block is added it cannot be altered or deleted, so the transaction history is permanent and tamper-proof.

Consensus mechanisms: blockchain networks use consensus mechanisms to agree on the validity of transactions. These mechanisms ensure that all nodes in the network reach a unanimous decision before adding a new block to the chain. Common consensus mechanisms include Proof of Work (PoW) and Proof of Stake (PoS).
book_errors: all nodes in the network reach a unanimous decision

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The book says all nodes must reach a unanimous decision. Consensus needs only a sufficient majority, not every node: in Proof of Work the majority of computing power decides, and in Proof of Stake a majority (often two thirds) of the stake; a new block is added even if some nodes are offline or dishonest.
